name: Detent
summary: A phone control panel whose switches thunk and whose sliders click past every step, with real buzz
about: A quick-controls screen built around feel. Each switch squishes when pressed, its knob stretches and then springs across while colour floods out from your finger, the tile gives a little thunk and its icon comes alive. The brightness and volume sliders click at every tenth, stretch like rubber at the ends and snap to the nearest step; brightness really dims the screen, airplane mode turns the radios off in a chain, and phones that can vibrate buzz at the strength you pick.
how: Tap Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Torch or Silent: the tile squishes, the colour spreads from where you pressed and the switch springs over with a thunk.
Drag the Brightness or Volume slider left and right: every 10 percent it clicks, the step mark pops, and on release it snaps to the nearest step. Tap a spot to jump there.
Turn on Airplane mode to watch Wi-Fi and Bluetooth switch off one after another; turn it off and they come back.
Pick Off, Soft or Strong under Haptics to change the buzz and how hard the tiles thunk. The black pill at the top shows each change.
Keyboard: Tab to a tile and press Space; on a slider use the arrow keys, Home and End. Your settings are remembered.
